items.stem: The Onyx Chamber runs 08:00-22:00. Reservations require 15-minute setup before the public start time. Cleanup requires 15 minutes after the public end. Public-facing time is limited to 5 hours maximum. Which reservation is valid?

blind_review.reasoning: The public intervals last 6 hours, 3 hours 45 minutes, 5 hours 45 minutes, and 5 hours 15 minutes respectively. Only B stays within the five-hour cap; its setup and cleanup also fit operating hours.

source.author_explanation: Public time is limited to 5 hours. Option A has 6 hours public time. Option C starts setup at 08:00 but chamber opens at 08:00, so setup cannot begin then. Option D has 5 hours 15 minutes public time. Option B has 3 hours 45 minutes public time, proper setup/cleanup timing, and fits within hours.

items.stem: The Amber Hall operates 10:00-18:00. If a reservation starts before 14:00, it may last up to 3 hours. If it starts at or after 14:00, it may last up to 2 hours. Which reservation is valid?

blind_review.reasoning: A begins before 14:00 but lasts 3 hours 30 minutes, exceeding three hours. B begins before 14:00 and lasts exactly three hours. C and D begin at or after 14:00 and each last 2 hours 30 minutes, exceeding two hours.

source.author_explanation: Starting before 14:00 allows 3 hours maximum; 11:00-14:30 exceeds this. Starting at or after 14:00 allows 2 hours maximum; 14:00-16:30 exceeds this, and 15:00-17:30 also exceeds this. 13:00-16:00 is exactly 3 hours, permitted for pre-14:00 starts.

items.stem: The Jade Gallery accepts reservations from 08:00 to 20:00. Priority members may book any slot. Standard members may only book slots starting at or after 12:00. Which reservation is valid for a standard member?

blind_review.reasoning: A starts at noon and ends within the gallery window. B extends past the 20:00 closing time; C and D start before the standard-member noon threshold.

source.author_explanation: Standard members are restricted to slots starting at or after 12:00. 08:00-10:00 starts too early. 11:30-13:30 starts before 12:00. 20:00-22:00 exceeds the gallery's 20:00 closing. Only 12:00-14:00 satisfies the standard member rule and operates within hours.

items.stem: The Special Exhibit opens at 13:00. Morning slots (before 13:00) are reserved for members only; afternoon slots require a guide fee of $50. A non-member arrives at 12:30 wanting the earliest possible slot. What applies?

choices.A: Can enter at 12:30 with no fee
choices.C: Must wait until 13:00 with no fee

blind_review.reasoning: The exhibit does not open to this non-member at 12:30. The earliest afternoon slot is at 13:00 and the afternoon guide fee is $50.

source.author_explanation: As a non-member, morning slots are unavailable. The earliest possible is 13:00, which triggers the afternoon guide fee requirement. Option A correctly combines both constraints.

items.stem: The North Wing opens at 09:00 and closes at 17:00. A reservation must end at least 30 minutes before closing. The maximum duration is 4 hours. Which 09:00 reservation is valid?

blind_review.reasoning: B runs 09:00–13:00 for four hours and finishes well before the 16:30 latest end. A and C exceed four hours. D claims four hours but its stated 09:00 start and 13:30 end span four and a half hours, so it is internally inconsistent and invalid.

source.author_explanation: The 30-minute buffer requires ending by 16:30, and the 4-hour limit applies. Only option A satisfies both: 09:00 to 13:00 is exactly 4 hours and ends before 16:30.

items.stem: The Rotunda has consecutive 90-minute slots starting at 09:00. A reservation can span multiple slots if continuous. The last slot must start by 16:30. Which reservation is impossible?

blind_review.reasoning: The 90-minute grid gives 15:00–16:30 and 16:30–18:00 as two consecutive slots, so A cannot end at 17:30. Three consecutive slots from 10:30 end at 15:00, not 14:30, so D is also impossible. B and C align with valid slots. Two choices satisfy “impossible.”

source.author_explanation: Slots are 09:00-10:30, 10:30-12:00, 12:00-13:30, 13:30-15:00, 15:00-16:30, 16:30-18:00. Option C (15:00-17:30) requires a slot starting at 16:30 to continue, but 16:30-18:00 is only 90 minutes; 15:00-17:30 is 150 minutes needing a non-existent 15:00-16:30 plus 16:30-18:00, but 15:00-16:30 exists. Rechecking: 15:00-16:30 and 16:30-18:00 gives exactly 15:00-18:00, not 17:30. Actually 15:00-17:30 cannot be formed from consecutive 90-minute slots. The last slot starts at 16:30, so 16:30-18:00 is valid. Option C's end time 17:30 doesn't align with slot boundaries.

items.stem: Room A and Room B share a single attendant. A booking in Room A from 09:00-12:00 blocks Room B during that window. Room B opens at 08:00 and closes at 16:00. When can Room B be reserved for 2 hours?

blind_review.reasoning: A starts when Room A’s blocking interval ends and finishes before Room B closes. B, C, and D each overlap the 09:00–12:00 blocked interval.

source.author_explanation: Room B is blocked 09:00-12:00 due to Room A's booking. A 2-hour reservation must avoid this window. Option D (12:00-14:00) starts exactly when the block ends and fits within 08:00-16:00.

items.stem: The Ruby Room opens at 09:00. Existing reservations take precedence: a new reservation is rejected if it overlaps any confirmed reservation. Confirmed: 10:00-12:00 and 14:00-16:00. Which new reservation is accepted?

blind_review.reasoning: A overlaps the 14:00–16:00 booking from 14:00 to 15:00; B overlaps it from 15:00 to 16:00; C overlaps the 10:00–12:00 booking from 11:00 to 12:00. D occupies the open interval 12:00–14:00, meeting existing reservations only at endpoints.

source.author_explanation: 11:00-13:00 overlaps 10:00-12:00. 13:00-15:00 overlaps 14:00-16:00. 15:00-17:00 overlaps 14:00-16:00. 12:00-14:00 touches but does not overlap either confirmed reservation, so it is accepted.

items.stem: The East Gallery opens at 10:00 and closes at 18:00. Reservations over 3 hours require 24-hour advance notice. A group submits a request at 09:00 today for tomorrow. Which reservation is accepted?

blind_review.reasoning: The request is submitted at 09:00 today. Every listed start time tomorrow is at least 25 hours later, so A, C, and D meet the 24-hour notice rule for durations over three hours. B is only two hours and needs no advance notice. All four also lie within opening hours.

source.author_explanation: The 24-hour notice is satisfied for tomorrow. The 4-hour reservation in option C fits within 10:00-18:00 and has proper notice. Option B violates the closing time (no buffer mentioned but 18:00 is exact closing), and D exceeds 3 hours without the explicit notice being for a long reservation.

items.stem: The Sapphire Wing opens at 09:00 and closes at 17:00. A reservation must end at least 30 minutes before closing. The maximum duration is 4 hours. Which reservation is valid?

blind_review.reasoning: A lasts five hours, exceeding the four-hour cap. B lasts four hours 15 minutes and ends after the 16:30 deadline. C lasts exactly four hours and ends at 14:00. D ends at closing rather than at least 30 minutes earlier.

source.author_explanation: The wing closes at 17:00, so reservations must end by 16:30. The 4-hour limit means 09:00-14:00 exceeds duration. 13:00-17:00 ends at closing time, violating the 30-minute buffer. 12:30-16:45 ends after 16:30. Only 10:00-14:00 fits both constraints.
